structure: Verified by WebFetch 2026-09-21: agents/contracts/ holds routes.json, gates.json, state-machine.json, roles.json (NOT role-policy.json), personas/, schemas/, plus per-provider conformance-evidence JSONs (codex, reasonix). 11 generated provider packages under agents/providers/ project the contracts. Generator script exposes renderCodexOutputs/renderReasonixOutputs/renderHarnessV2Outputs. README cites 25 personas + 18 frameworks as 'complete'; commit messages cite '32 role projections' elsewhere (the overcount the prior verdict propagated). NOT 550 hand-authored artifacts.

decisions.fork_ground: Generation coupling: forking means adopting the generator script + 11 output trees with machine-owned compiled-block markers. The corpus has no compiler pipeline; adopting one would invert the audit model (curated skills become generated projections). provenance.json:1620 already rejects vendor-tool skills on staleness/maintenance grounds.

agents/contracts/routes.json.evidence: directory listing confirmed; contents not yet read in full.
agents/contracts/routes.json.note: adopt-rule: 'file count, repository size, failed attempt, or preference for more agents never selects a larger route'. The corpus's escalation rules are scattered (dispatching-parallel-agents for parallelism, brainstorming for option count, writing-plans for plan depth); no single rule refuses upward routing on those four signals. This is the most distinctive autoprompt rule — likely the strongest candidate for adoption.
agents/contracts/routes.json.caveat: destination owed. verifying-before-completion owns completion evidence; this rule is about route CLASSIFICATION, which is upstream. A new lightweight 'route-classification' skill may be the right home. Decide after reading routes.json in full.

agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.evidence: directory listing confirmed; contents not yet read in full.
agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.note: adopt-rule: 'freeze-before-check + state-machine-driven retry with non-resetting limits'. Structurally similar to verifying-before-completion's Gate Function (IDENTIFY/RUN/READ/VERIFY) but the corpus's Gate Function does not pin retry-budget discipline. The non-resetting-limits property is a real addition: the corpus's verifying-before-completion does not currently say what to do after N failures.
agents/contracts/gates.json + state-mach.caveat: scope of 'failure' is ambiguous — agent failure vs. check failure vs. tool failure. Must be specified before adopting. The combination of gates.json AND state-machine.json suggests these are two related contracts; read both before deciding whether to fold them as one rule or two.

agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.evidence: directory listing confirmed; structure is per-provider conformance evidence JSONs, which matches the 'refuse without current provider conformance evidence' rule.
agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.note: adopt-rule: 'refuse any required capability without current provider conformance evidence'. harness-bridge comes closest (it pins --permission-mode plan and --fork-session) but the rule is about CAPABILITY discovery, not ARG translation. The autoprompt model pins per-provider live conformance evidence; the corpus currently relies on static capability flags.
agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-.caveat: harness-bridge already enforces capability evidence by setting stdin:true/false and refusing CLIs that lack stream-json. The new rule is more general — apply to any capability, not just stream-json. Verify the existing capability flags meet the autoprompt bar before adopting the rule.

agents/contracts/personas/ (25 personas.evidence: directory listing confirmed; README cites 25 personas + 18 frameworks; commits cite 32 role projections (overcount).
agents/contracts/personas/ (25 personas.note: reject: the corpus already names personas by skill (reviewing-for-bloat, verifying-before-completion, dispatching-parallel-agents). The autoprompt personas/ tree is provider-coupled and overlaps with skills it would have to displace.

agents/providers/* (11 provider packages.evidence: directory listing of providers/ (claude, codex, omp, opencode, kilo, vscode, prime, deepseek, hermes, grok, reasonix).
agents/providers/* (11 provider packages.note: reject: 11 generated provider packages are projections of the 7 contracts. Adopting them would adopt a generation pipeline the corpus does not have.

agents/contracts/README.md (architecture.note: reject: the architecture framing ('provider-neutral source of truth, generator projects into provider packages') is a packaging model the corpus does not use. audacioustux/agents ships curated Markdown + Python CLI.

summary.fork: no (ground: generation coupling, not file count)

next_steps: Read agents/contracts/routes.json in full to resolve the destination for the no-fallback-route rule (verifying-before-completion vs new route-classification skill).
Read agents/contracts/gates.json AND state-machine.json in full to specify what 'failure' means under non-resetting retry limits.
Read agents/contracts/codex-live-conformance-evidence.json to confirm the conformance-evidence rule generalises beyond stream-json and meets the harness-bridge bar.

If all three resolve to clear adopt-rule destinations, file 3 PRs targeting verifying-before-completion, harness-bridge, and one new skill (route-classification). Update this ledger with landedIn SHAs.

key_corrections: Decision A (fork) and Decision B (extract) are orthogonal; blending them weakens both halves.
The 550-file claim was an overcount. Real structure is 7 hand-authored contracts + 11 generated provider packages.

The corpus has a documented audit schema (docs/audits/cursor-plugins/README.md:47-50) with disposition/status/note/evidence/landedIn + caveat; ~20% of adopt-rule recommendations historically fail scrutiny. The proposed verdict skipped this entirely.
Generation coupling (adopting a compiler + machine-owned compiled-block markers) is a sharper fork argument than file count or vendor-paths.
AGENTS.md absence is conditional on provenance.json:1598, not a contradiction. The Python CLI fabrication was unfounded.
